meta.title: Kiko Light Palette
meta.scope: palette only: no app code. Dark values are copied from the code and checked by check-dark.mjs.
meta.tokenCountNote: theme.ts has 21 color lines in darkTheme.colors: 19 string tokens plus 2 palette references (entityColors, chartSeries). The research said 19, which is right for string tokens.
meta.rationale: Light values start from Apple's iOS light system colors. Where a system value fails WCAG 2.2 AA on the real backgrounds (systemBlue 4.0:1, systemGreen 2.2:1, systemRed 3.6:1, secondaryLabel 3.5:1), the hue is kept and the lightness is lowered until the pair passes. The check is contrast.mjs.

A.label: Grouped gray page, white cards (iOS Settings look)

B.label: Mid-gray thumb that clears 3:1 like the dark one

background.use: Screen fill, tab bar fill (pinned), navigation background and card, flat-fallback base under tonal buttons. Light: systemGroupedBackground, so white cards stand out without a shadow. The launch screen is black, so a saved Light shows about 300 ms of black, then a fade.

surface.use: Solid content Card, chart cards, filter menu, date range field, disabled field fill, opaque GlassSurface base. Dark is a composite of translucent glass over black; light is white (secondarySystemGroupedBackground), not a composite, because white over a gray page cannot be reached by a translucent white.

surfaceTranslucent.use: See-through GlassSurface backdrop and its non-glass fill. Over the light page it composites to about #FAFAFC, 5 levels from the solid card.

surfaceTranslucentStrong.use: Home transaction card backdrop: a stronger pin so the card drifts less in lightness while scrolling.

surfaceWashStrong.use: Neutral overlay drawn on top of the finished translucentStrong glass. Dark darkens it; light whitens it (a black wash on light glass would look dirty gray). Same alpha, same job: a visible step toward the opaque side.

surfaceHigh.use: Raised pill: secondary Button fill, Switch off track, sync progress track, read-only notice, disabled field border, glassTint of the secondary footer button. Light: systemGray5.

fieldBackground.use: Fill of an editable input: TextField and FieldTrigger (and so every select, currency, wallet and credential field built on them). Dark is unfilled, as approved. Light is white, lighter than the gray page and sheet (#F2F2F7); the hairline border keeps a field readable on a white card. A disabled field still uses surface with the surfaceHigh border and 0.5 opacity.

sheetBackground.use: Opaque base of a presented BottomSheet (iOS < 26 fallback and flat paths). A grouped base one level under the white cards and pills on it.

segmentSelected.use: Selected thumb of SegmentedControl. Dark is tuned to clear 3:1 against its track. Light is the native iOS white thumb, ruled by the user on 2026-11-03 (decision 2, option A). The user accepted that the thumb-to-track pair FAILs 3:1 (about 1.15:1 to 1.28:1); the 600-weight selected label also marks the selection.

textPrimary.use: Body text, titles, neutral amounts, secondary Button label, symbol tint default, TextField text, color-picker selected ring, header tint.

textSecondary.use: Captions, labels, placeholders, disabled calendar days, spinner, tab bar inactive, chart axis text and reference line. Light keeps Apple's secondaryLabel hue but 0.78 alpha, not 0.60: at 0.60 it is 3.4:1 on white and fails AA for caption text.

accent.use: Primary Button fill, selected chip/row fill, Switch on track, links and accent text, calendar today/arrows/selected day, tab bar active, navigation primary, glassTint of the primary footer button. Light: systemBlue #007AFF is only 4.0:1 under white text; #0066E6 keeps the 213 degree hue and gives 5.19:1.

onAccent.use: Label, glyph and thumb on a filled accent or negative surface. Always white in both schemes.

positive.use: Positive amounts (MoneyText), net-worth line above the start value, positive sync status. Light: a teal-leaning green so it stays apart from the red for color-blind users (see computed.json cvd).

negative.use: Negative amounts, destructive Button fill, net-worth line below the start value, errors, destructiveTonal label, glassTint of the destructive footer button. Light: darker than systemRed so the red label still passes on its own 12% tint.

negativeSubtle.use: Fill of the destructiveTonal Button and its flat footer fallback. Light: 12% of the light negative; the fill is a visible pink (#F8E0E3 over the white card), not the old faint tint, and the red label still passes on it.

neutralSubtle.use: Segmented track, unselected chip and day-of-month chip, secondaryTonal Button fill and its flat footer fallback. Light: iOS tertiarySystemFill at its light alpha.

border.use: Hairline on cards, fields, dividers, sheet handle edge, chart gridlines, two-pane divider, navigation border. Light: opaqueSeparator.

scrim.use: Dismiss scrim and tint of the live-blur scrim behind a BottomSheet on iOS 26+. Light is lighter: the glass sheet samples this dimmed screen, and 0.4 black over a white page turns the sample mid-gray (#999999) and drags the sheet text contrast down. Device check needed.

scrimFallback.use: Dismiss scrim for iOS < 26 (opaque sheet; nothing samples it). Heavier than the glass scrim, as on dark, but 0.15 lower because black dims a white screen more than a black one.

white.note: Graphite. A white tile would vanish on a white card. Default for bank accounts and card holdings.

yellow.note: Pale gold tile with a black glyph; its darker mark (markSwatches) carries lines and bare glyph tints.

indigo.note: Lighter than blue by about 15 L*, so the two stay apart for color-blind users.

yellow.note: Same hex as the entity yellow: one light set for entity and category tiles.

indigo.note: Lighter than blue by about 15 L*, so the two stay apart for color-blind users.

swatchSets.entityRule: Tile fill, v3.1: one light set for entity and category tiles. The glyph is computed (white or black, whichever contrasts more on the base), at least 4.5:1 on the base and 3:1 on the worst gradient stop, except that orange, teal and indigo take white by the user ruling of 2026-11-09; orange (4.16) and indigo (4.39) sit below the 4.5:1 base floor on purpose and keep the 3:1 stop floor, teal meets both. The tile need not clear 3:1 on the page (waived, ruling R6); lines and bare glyph tints use the mark shade instead.
swatchSets.categoryRule: Same hexes as the entity set (ruling R1). Slices and bars paint the tile hex with no edge; a trend line, its legend dot and a bare glyph tint paint the mark shade, at least 3.05:1 on the page (#F2F2F7) and on the card (#FFFFFF).
swatchSets.whatDiffers: Nothing: entitySwatches.light equals categorySwatches.light for all 14 keys. The mark shade (markSwatches) differs from the tile only for yellow, mint, violet, pink and gray, the pale tiles whose own hex is under 3.05:1 on the page or the card.

chartSeries.invariant: The light series is a subset of categorySwatches.light (same rule as dark: the category color picker rings the swatch of an uncolored category's fallback hue).

netWorthAreaOpacity.use: Positive band stop next to the line. Same alpha; the fill color is the light positive.

netWorthNegativeAreaOpacity.use: Negative band stop next to the line. Dark needs 0.5 because blending toward black loses the color; on white the same alpha already reads, so light uses 0.3 (composite #F3B3B9 over white).

chartParameters.background: surface (every chart sits in a Card)
chartParameters.pie: slices fill = category color (resolveCategoryColor); legend dot = same hex

defaults.providerColors: none: no bank or crypto provider in src/ carries its own brand color; accounts take the kind default.

storedHexMap.rule: Store the dark hex as the canonical value. Accounts and holdings read the entity map; categories read the category map. The two maps cannot be merged: the same dark hex has a different light hex per set.

legacyLightEraHex.note: NOT BUILT (spec D3, C4). The old picker could store a light hex in the two-day window 2026-09-07 to 09-09. Such a value takes the cannotMap rule. This table stays for reference only.

cannotMap: Any #RRGGBB that is not one of the 14 dark swatch hexes (a hand-edited or imported .kiko file). Rule: keep the hue and saturation, lower HSL lightness in 1% steps until the contrast to white is at least 3.4. Unchanged if it already passes. Test fixtures such as #112233 and #00FF00 appear only in migration tests.
null or empty string: not stored data; resolveEntityColor falls to the kind or type default, which maps by swatch key.

3-digit hex, rgb() strings or uppercase/lowercase variants: isValidHex only accepts #RRGGBB, so these already fall back to the default. Lookup must lower-case or upper-case the key first (the dark palette is upper-case).

gradient.note: Same numbers. Top stop = lightenHex(base, 15), bottom = darkenHex(base, 20), both from the light swatch.

glyph.rule: Light (v3.1): computed, no per-swatch flag. The glyph is white (onAccent) or black (glyphOnLightTile #000000), whichever contrasts more on the base hue; at least 4.5:1 on the base and 3:1 on the worst gradient stop (+15% / -20%). Black on yellow, mint, violet, pink and gray; white on the rest, including orange, teal and indigo by the user ruling of 2026-11-09 (orange and indigo sit below 4.5:1 on purpose). Dark keeps its rule: white glyph unless contrast(white, base) < 3, then black; the dark glyph choices do not change.

notification.source: inherited from @react-navigation/native DarkTheme; light value = negative

colorSchemeProp.note: The dark value is the code today: colorScheme is hard-coded dark in glass-surface.component.tsx and bottom-sheet.component.tsx. Set 5 changes both sites to "system" (spec D5, C13; measured in probes N1 and N2), so the prop inherits the window scheme in both schemes.

other.symbolTints: tone tokens: textPrimary, textSecondary, accent, positive, negative, onAccent; or an explicit entity/category hex on a bare glyph (TransactionCard, trend filter rows).
nativeChromeNotPalette: RefreshControl, date and time pickers, alerts: no tint, follow the window
Launch screen: fixed black by decision
App icons: out of scope here
Status bar: no StatusBar code in src/, follows the window style
Launch screen text is white on black in LaunchScreen.storyboard:22,26
other.providerColorsNote: grep of src/ found no bank or crypto provider brand color; monobank.types black/white are card types, not UI colors

knownFailures.reason: Native iOS white thumb on a faint track; the selected label is also 600 weight. Accepted by the user 2026-11-03 (decision 2, option A, native white thumb); the mid-gray alternative that reaches 3:1 was declined.
Apple off track is a faint gray by design; the thumb position and the accent on-color carry the state. Dark has the same FAIL (1.35). Fix would change both schemes.
Native UISwitch draws a shadow under the white thumb; the dark pair passes only because its track is dark.
DARK VALUE, NOTE ONLY: white on the bright dark accent/negative is 3.4 to 3.7:1 for 16/600 text. Dark is locked and was not changed.
DARK VALUE, NOTE ONLY: the red label on its tint over the sheet is 4.05:1. Dark is locked.
DARK VALUE, NOTE ONLY: the code comment tunes the thumb for surface and black, not the sheet (2.76:1). Dark is locked.
DARK VALUE, NOTE ONLY: the glyph rule measures the base hue, so the lightened top stop of brown, violet and red tiles is just under 3:1 at the very top edge.
